Ito pala ay isang pating at isda, hindi balyena!

Kini diay usa ka iho ug isda, dili balyena!

Why is each whale shark's pattern unique?

Each whale shark has its own pattern of white and yellow spots—like a fingerprint, no two are ever exactly the same!

Bakit natatangi ang batik ng bawat butanding?

May sariling batik na puti at dilaw ang bawat butanding—gaya ng fingerprint, walang dalawang magkatulad ang pattern!
copy.bis:
Nganong talagsaon ang porma sa matag tuki?

Ang matag tuki adunay kaugalingong puti ug dalag nga porma—sama sa fingerprint, walay duha ka managsama!

Do whales sing just for fun?

Not really—whale songs are actually a way of communicating with a purpose, not just music for entertainment like people think.
copy.tl:

Hindi pala—ang kanta ng balyena ay isang paraan ng pakikipag-usap na may dahilan, hindi lang basta tugtog para aliwin.

Nakita ni Robert Hooke ang mga unang 'cell' sa isang manipis na hiwa ng cork, ang balat ng cork-oak na puno!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang gitan-aw ni Robert Hooke?

Nakita ni Robert Hooke ang unang mga 'cell' sa nipis nga hiwa sa cork, ang panit sa kahoy nga cork-oak!

Sumala sa cell theory, ang tanang buhing butang gilangkuban sa usa o daghang selula!

Kini mao ang kasarangang gitas-on sa ibabaw sa dagat, nga gigamit isip sukdanan sa tanan!

A species is one kind of living thing whose members can breed with each other and have offspring that can also breed — all humans are one species!

Ang species ay isang uri ng buhay na bagay na maaaring magparami sa isa't isa at magkaroon ng anak na kaya ring magparami — lahat ng tao ay iisang species!

Ang species usa ka matang sa buhi nga butang nga makahimo og pagsanay tali sa usag usa ug makabaton og anak nga makasanay usab — ang tanang tawo usa ra ka species!

The wheel was first made in ancient Mesopotamia! This round invention completely changed how people travel and move heavy things.

Ang gulong ay unang ginawa sa sinaunang Mesopotamia! Ang bilog na imbentong ito ay lubos na nagbago sa pagbiyahe at paglipat ng mga bagay.

Ang ligid (gulong) unang gihimo sa karaang Mesopotamia! Kining lingin nga imbento nag-usab sa pagbiyahe ug pagbalhin sa mga butang.

Si Galileo Galilei! Siya ang nakatuklas ng apat na malalaking buwan ng Jupiter gamit ang kanyang telescope.
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang nakadiskobre sa upat ka dagkong bulan sa Jupiter?

Si Galileo Galilei! Siya ang nakadiskobre sa upat ka dagkong bulan sa Jupiter gamit ang iyang telescope.

Kinsa ang miingon nga tanang selula gikan sa selula?

Gidugang ni Rudolf Virchow niadtong 1855 nga ang tanang selula gikan sa nag-una nang selula — "omnis cellula e cellula."

assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why animal parents care for their young (feeding, warmth, guarding) but does not identify the basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter). It shares the broad topic of living things but provides no direct instructional support for identifying basic needs.

copy.en: Many animal parents care for their babies because they're still weak and can't survive alone — they feed them, keep them warm, and guard them until they grow strong.
copy.tl: Maraming hayop na magulang ang nag-aalaga sa kanilang mga anak dahil mahina pa ito at hindi pa kayang mabuhay mag-isa — pinapakain, iniinitan, at binabantayan sila hanggang lumakas.
copy.bis: Daghang mananap nga ginikanan mag-atiman sa ilang mga anak kay huyang pa kini ug dili pa makabuhi mag-inusara — pakan-on, init-initan, ug bantayan sila hangtod molig-on.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: chasing and wrestling helps young animals practice hunting, fighting, and getting along
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses young animals' play behavior, not the stages of an animal life cycle, and it does not use a flow chart as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: chasing and wrestling helps young animals practice hunting, fighting, and getting along
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about animal play and practice behaviors; it does not describe outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor their roles in movement and gathering food.

copy.en:
Why do puppies and kittens wrestle so much?

It's not just play — chasing and wrestling helps young animals practice hunting, fighting, and getting along for when they grow up.
copy.tl:
Bakit palaging naghahabulan ang mga tuta at kuting?

Hindi lang ito laro — ang paghahabulan at pagkukulitan ay pagsasanay ng mga batang hayop sa panghuhuli, paglaban, at pakikisama paglaki nila.
copy.bis:
Ngano kanunay maggukod ang mga itoy ug kuring?

Dili lang kini dula — ang paggukod ug pagdula-dula pagbansay sa mga batan-ong mananap sa pagpangayam, pagpakig-away, ug pakig-uban kung modako na sila.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A bubble pops when its thin soapy film dries out or gets touched
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify objects, activities, or natural events observed in their local environment that can be explained by science
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why bubbles pop, which is a natural event that could be explained by science, but it does not ask students to identify objects, activities, or natural events that can be explained by science. It provides an explanation rather than supporting the identification skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the air inside escapes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air inside a bubble, which is a gas, but it does not teach that matter exists in three states (solid, liquid, gas) or help identify these states. The mention of air is incidental and does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Why do bubbles pop?

A bubble pops when its thin soapy film dries out or gets touched — the surface breaks and the air inside escapes!
copy.tl:
Bakit pumuputok ang bula?

Pumuputok ang bula kapag natuyo ang manipis na pelikula ng tubig-sabon nito o nahawakan — nasisira ang ibabaw at tumatakas ang hangin sa loob!
copy.bis:
Nganong mobuto ang bula?

Mobuto ang bula kon mauga ang nipis nga pelikula sa tubig-sabon niini o mahikapan — maguba ang gawas ug moikyas ang hangin sa sulod!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fluid inside our ears helps us balance
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the ear and balance, which is not one of the five body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) named in the competency. It shares the broad topic of human body function but does not directly support the stated skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fluid inside our ears helps us balance
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about observing and describing outer body parts of animals (head, legs, wings) and their role in movement and food gathering. The card is about inner ear fluid and balance, not outer body parts or movement/food gathering.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fluid inside our ears helps us balance
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about characteristics of living things: grow, respond, reproduce. The card explains dizziness from spinning, which does not address growth, response, or reproduction.

copy.en:
Why do we feel dizzy after spinning around?

Fluid inside our ears helps us balance; when we spin fast, it keeps moving even after we stop, so it feels like the room is still spinning.
copy.tl:
Bakit tayo nahihilo pagkatapos umikot?

May likido sa loob ng ating tainga na tumutulong sa balanse; kapag mabilis tayong umiikot, patuloy itong gumagalaw kahit huminto na tayo, kaya parang umiikot pa rin ang paligid.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga malipong ta human moliyok?

Adunay likido sa sulod sa atong dalunggan nga makatabang sa balanse; kon paspas ta moliyok, kini nagpadayon sa paglihok bisan human ta mohunong, mao nga murag nagtuyok pa ang palibot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A nerve runs close to your skin there — bump it and you feel a jolt like electricity
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why hitting the elbow causes a tingling sensation due to a nerve near the skin. It does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) as a general concept; the tingling is a specific physiological response, not framed as a characteristic of living things. It shares the broad subject of living things but provides no direct instructional support for this competency.

copy.en:
Why does hitting your elbow tingle?

A nerve runs close to your skin there — bump it and you feel a jolt like electricity, tingling all the way to your fingers. That's the 'funny bone'!
copy.tl:
Bakit kumikiliti pag naumpog ang siko?

May nerbiyong dumadaan malapit sa balat sa siko — kapag naumpog, parang nakuryente ka at kumikiliti hanggang sa daliri. Kaya tinatawag itong 'funny bone'!
copy.bis:
Ngano mangurog kon mabunggo ang siko?

Adunay nerbiyo nga duol sa panit sa siko — kon mabunggo, mura'g gikuryente ug manuhot hangtod sa mga tudlo. Mao nga gitawag kining 'funny bone'!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A pencil eraser is made of slightly tacky rubber!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions 'tacky' as a property of rubber, but the competency requires describing physical properties such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. The card's focus is on how the eraser removes graphite through adhesion, not on describing the physical properties of solid materials. It shares vocabulary but does not directly teach the skill of describing physical properties.

copy.en: A pencil eraser is made of slightly tacky rubber! When you rub it, the dark graphite sticks to the rubber and is carried away, making the writing disappear.
copy.tl: Ang pambura ay gawa sa slightly tacky na goma! Kapag kinuskos mo ito, dumidikit ang dark graphite sa goma at natatangay palayo, kaya nawawala ang sulat.
copy.bis: Ang pang-papas hinimo sa slightly tacky nga goma! Kon kuskuson nimo, mopilit ang dark graphite sa goma ug madala palayo, mao nga mawala ang sinulat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Soap molecules are like tiny matchmakers — one end loves water, the other loves oil!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how soap interacts with water and oil to remove grease, but does not describe uniform vs non-uniform mixtures, solutions, or suspensions. It only touches on the general idea of mixing substances, not the classification or examples required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: one end loves water, the other loves oil!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water and oil but does not identify the roles of solute and solvent in a solution. It does not discuss dissolving, the solute being the substance dissolved, or the solvent as the dissolving medium. The soap action is about emulsification, not solution chemistry.

copy.en: Soap molecules are like tiny matchmakers — one end loves water, the other loves oil! So soap grabs grease and dirt off your skin or dishes, and water rinses it all away!
copy.tl: Ang mga molekula ng sabon ay parang maliliit na matchmaker — ang isang dulo ay mahilig sa tubig, ang kabilang dulo sa langis! Kaya hinahagilap ng sabon ang mantika at dumi sa balat o pinggan, at tinatangay ng tubig kapag binanlawan!
copy.bis: Ang mga molekula sa sabon sama sa gagmay nga matchmaker — ang usa ka tumoy ganahan sa tubig, ang pikas tumoy sa lana! Maong mokuha ang sabon sa mantika ug hugaw sa panit o plato, ug mabanlasan kini sa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sugar tastes sweet because its molecules fit special sensors on your tongue! They send a 'sweet' signal to your brain to recognize energy-rich food.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes taste perception via tongue sensors and a brain signal, which relates to the sensory/nervous system, not any of the five systems named in G4-L-1 (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory). It shares the broad topic of human body function but does not directly support the listed systems.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sugar tastes sweet because its molecules fit special sensors on your tongue! They send a 'sweet' signal to your brain to recognize energy-rich food.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a sensory response (tasting sweetness) and recognition of energy-rich food, but does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). While responding to stimuli is a characteristic of living things, the card does not teach that concept; it only gives an example of a response without linking it to the competency's focus.

copy.en: Sugar tastes sweet because its molecules fit special sensors on your tongue! They send a 'sweet' signal to your brain to recognize energy-rich food.
copy.tl: Matamis ang asukal dahil ang molecules niito ay pumapasok sa special sensors sa dila! Nagpapadala ito ng 'sweet' signal sa utak para makilala ang energy-rich food.
copy.bis: Tam-is ang asukal kay ang molecules niini mosulod sa special sensors sa dila! Nagpadala kini og 'sweet' signal sa utok aron mailhan ang energy-rich food.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the sun's rays fall almost straight down the whole year
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a physical model or use drawings to demonstrate how the tilt of the Earth relative to its orbit around the Sun affects the intensity of sunlight absorbed by different areas of Earth over a year
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why the tropics stay warm because sunlight is direct, but it does not mention Earth's tilt, its orbit, or how tilt affects sunlight intensity over a year. It also does not use a physical model or drawings as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Places in the tropics, like the Philippines, stay warm all year
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different seasons in the Philippines and suggest activities that are appropriate for each season
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that the Philippines has no winter and stays warm all year, but it does not describe the different seasons in the Philippines or suggest activities appropriate for each season. It only touches on the absence of a cold season, not the full competency.

copy.en: Places in the tropics, like the Philippines, stay warm all year! They sit near the equator where the sun's rays fall almost straight down the whole year, so there is no winter.
copy.tl: Ang mga lugar sa tropiko, tulad ng Pilipinas, ay mainit buong taon! Malapit sila sa ekwador kung saan halos tuwid na bumabagsak ang sikat ng araw buong taon, kaya walang taglamig doon.
copy.bis: Ang mga dapit sa tropiko, sama sa Pilipinas, init tibuok tuig! Duol sila sa ekwador diin halos tul-id nga mahulog ang kahayag sa adlaw sa tibuok tuig, maong walay tingtugnaw didto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water dissolves the substances it is attracted to, like sugar and salt!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses what water dissolves but does not describe uniform/non-uniform mixtures, solutions, or suspensions, nor classify examples as such. It only touches on solubility, which is related vocabulary but not the competency's focus.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water dissolves the substances it is attracted to, like sugar and salt!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water dissolving sugar and salt, which are solute-solvent examples, but it never identifies the roles of solute and solvent, nor uses the terms. It does not directly teach the role of solute and solvent in a solution.

copy.en: Water dissolves the substances it is attracted to, like sugar and salt! But it leaves whole the substances it cannot pull apart, like sand.
copy.tl: Natutunaw ng tubig ang mga sangkap na nahihila nito, tulad ng asukal at asin! Pero iniiwan nitong buo ang mga hindi nito kayang hilahin, tulad ng buhangin.
copy.bis: Matunaw sa tubig ang mga sangkap nga mabira niini, sama sa asukal ug asin! Apan ibilin niini nga buo ang mga dili niini mabira, sama sa balas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A chemical slowly builds up in the brain all day while we're awake — sleep clears it away and restores our energy!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific sleep-regulating mechanism (buildup of a brain chemical and its clearance by sleep), but does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems, nor mention its indicators (body temperature, glucose level, blood pressure). It shares the broad theme of body regulation but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
Why do we feel sleepy at night?

A chemical slowly builds up in the brain all day while we're awake — sleep clears it away and restores our energy!
copy.tl:
Bakit tayo naaantok sa gabi?

Unti-unting naiipon ang isang kemikal sa utak habang gising tayo buong araw — inaalis ito ng katulog at ibinabalik ang enerhiya!
copy.bis:
Nganong katulgon ta sa gabii?

Hinay-hinayng matipon ang usa ka kemikal sa utok samtang nagmata ta tibuok adlaw — kuhaon kini sa pagtulog ug ibalik ang kusog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Vitamins are nutrients your body needs in tiny amounts to stay healthy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses vitamins as nutrients needed in small amounts, which is about nutrition, not the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter) that G3-L-6 targets. It does not directly support identifying basic needs.

copy.en:
Why does your body need vitamins?

Vitamins are nutrients your body needs in tiny amounts to stay healthy — vitamin C from fruit, vitamin D from sunlight, and vitamin A for clear eyesight.
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangan ng katawan ang bitamina?

Ang mga bitamina ay sustansyang kailangan ng katawan sa maliliit na dami para manatiling malusog — vitamin C mula sa prutas, vitamin D mula sa sikat ng araw, at vitamin A para sa malinaw na paningin.
copy.bis:
Nganong gikinahanglan sa lawas ang bitamina?

Ang mga bitamina mao ang sustansya nga gikinahanglan sa lawas sa gagmayng gidaghanon aron magpabiling himsog — vitamin C gikan sa prutas, vitamin D gikan sa sidlak sa adlaw, ug vitamin A alang sa tin-aw nga panan-aw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Yawning helps us take a deep breath
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a deep breath but does not identify or describe the parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or how they work. It only touches on a respiratory-related behavior, not the competency's content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Yawning helps us take a deep breath
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe how any human body system works, including the respiratory system. It only mentions yawning and a deep breath, which is not a description of the system's function.

copy.en:
Why do we yawn?

Yawning helps us take a deep breath that may cool the brain and wake us up — and yawns are contagious, spreading when we see someone else yawn!
copy.tl:
Bakit tayo humihikab?

Ang paghikab ay tumutulong sa ating huminga nang malalim, na maaaring palamigin ang utak at gisingin tayo — at nakakahawa ang hikab, lumalaganap kapag may nakita tayong humihikab!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga maghuy-ab ta?

Ang paghuy-ab motabang nato sa pagginhawa og lawom, nga tingali makapabugnaw sa utok ug makapukaw kanato — ug makatakod ang huy-ab, kaylap kon adunay makita tang naghuy-ab!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Talinum is a wild green that grows easily in backyards and along roadsides.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a list or draw up a table with examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, such as a garden, rice field, seashore, and mangrove swamp
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a plant and a general location (backyards, roadsides) but does not make a list or table of animals and plants in a named habitat, which is the required format and action of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Its thick, soft leaves are cooked like spinach
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions leaves but does not describe observing outer plant parts (leaves, roots, stems) or their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil. It only notes that leaves are edible, which is not the competency's focus.

copy.en: Talinum is a wild green that grows easily in backyards and along roadsides. Its thick, soft leaves are cooked like spinach, so in English it's called "Philippine spinach."
copy.tl: Ang talinum ay halamang-ligaw na madaling tumutubo sa bakuran at sa tabi ng daan. Makapal at malambot ang dahon nito na niluluto tulad ng spinach, kaya "Philippine spinach" ang tawag dito sa Ingles.
copy.bis: Ang talinum usa ka ihalas nga utanon nga sayon motubo sa nataran ug daplin sa dalan. Baga ug humok ang dahon niini nga giluto sama sa spinach, mao nga "Philippine spinach" ang tawag niini sa Iningles.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A smart wind erosion solution!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes windbreaks as a method to prevent wind erosion, but does not demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials. It only mentions wind erosion as a problem, not the process of transport.

copy.en: Farmers plant rows of tall trees called windbreaks! These tree walls block strong winds, keeping soil safe and crops healthy. A smart wind erosion solution!
copy.tl: Nagtanim ang mga magsasaka ng hanay ng matataas na puno na tinatawag na windbreaks! Hinaharang nito ang malakas na hangin, pinoprotektahan ang lupa at pananim. Matalinong solusyon sa wind erosion!
copy.bis: Nagtanom ang mga mag-uuma og laray sa taas nga kahoy nga gitawag og windbreaks! Gipugngan niini ang kusog nga hangin, gipanalipdan ang yuta ug tanom. Maayong solusyon sa wind erosion!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Global atmospheric circulation is shaped by three main cells!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card names the three circulation cells but does not explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere. It lacks any description of solar heating, energy transfer, or the mechanism linking solar energy to atmospheric processes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: There's the Hadley cell near the equator, the Ferrel cell in middle latitudes, and the polar cell.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how solar energy contributes to the occurrence of land and sea breezes, monsoons, and the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Hadley cell, which is related to the ITCZ, but it does not explain how solar energy contributes to land and sea breezes, monsoons, or the ITCZ. It only names the cells without describing the causal role of solar energy.

copy.en: Global atmospheric circulation is shaped by three main cells! There's the Hadley cell near the equator, the Ferrel cell in middle latitudes, and the polar cell.
copy.tl: Ang global atmospheric circulation ay hinuhubog ng tatlong pangunahing cell! May Hadley cell malapit sa equator, Ferrel cell sa gitnang latitudes, at polar cell.
copy.bis: Ang global atmospheric circulation gihubog sa tulo ka nag-unang cell! Adunay Hadley cell duol sa equator, Ferrel cell sa gitnang latitudes, ug polar cell.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: typhoons are huge (hundreds of kilometres) and last days!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card only contrasts tornadoes and typhoons by size, duration, and wind speed. It does not explain how typhoons develop or why the Philippines is prone to typhoons, which are the actions in the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: typhoons are huge (hundreds of kilometres) and last days!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions typhoons but does not describe typical weather conditions before, during, or after a tropical cyclone. It only gives a size/duration comparison with tornadoes.

copy.en: Tornadoes are small (a few hundred metres), last minutes, with faster winds — while typhoons are huge (hundreds of kilometres) and last days!
copy.tl: Ang mga tornado ay maliit (ilang daang metro), ilang minuto lang, at mas mabilis ang hangin — habang ang mga typhoon ay napakalaki (daan-daang kilometro) at tumatagal ng mga araw!
copy.bis: Ang mga tornado gamay (pipila ka gatus ka metro), minuto ra, ug mas paspas ang hangin — samtang ang mga typhoon dako kaayo (gatusan ka kilometro) ug molungtad og mga adlaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A wind turbine uses the wind's power to spin its large blades and make electricity
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how high voltage electricity from power plants is generated and safely distributed to industries, businesses, and homes, including the role of substations (grid stations), and electric meters
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that a wind turbine generates electricity. It does not describe high voltage generation, safe distribution to industries/businesses/homes, substations, or electric meters, which are the core of G10-F-9.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A wind turbine uses the wind's power to spin its large blades and make electricity
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to evaluate how renewable and non-renewable generation of electricity in the Philippines impacts human activities and the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a renewable electricity source (wind) but does not evaluate impacts on human activities or the environment, nor does it involve gathering information from secondary sources. It is only a basic factual statement about wind turbines.

copy.en: A wind turbine uses the wind's power to spin its large blades and make electricity, just like in Bangui, Ilocos Norte!
copy.tl: Ginagamit ng wind turbine ang lakas ng hangin para paikutin ang malalaking blades nito at gumawa ng kuryente, tulad sa Bangui, Ilocos Norte!
copy.bis: Ang wind turbine mogamit sa kusog sa hangin aron tuyokon ang dagkong blades niini ug mohimo og kuryente, sama sa Bangui, Ilocos Norte!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The faster the plane moves, the more air rushes over its wings, making the lift even greater!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card uses the idea of speed as a cause of greater lift, but it does not teach that speed is how far an object moves in a given time. It provides no definition or measurement of speed, so it does not directly support G4-F-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The faster the plane moves, the more air rushes over its wings, making the lift even greater!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces act between objects and can be measured
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions lift, which is a force, but it does not identify that forces act between objects or that forces can be measured. It only states a qualitative relationship between speed and lift, so it does not directly support G7-F-1.

copy.en: The faster the plane moves, the more air rushes over its wings, making the lift even greater!
copy.tl: Habang bumibilis ang eroplano, mas maraming hangin ang dumadaloy sa pakpak, kaya mas lumalaki ang lift!
copy.bis: Samtang mopaspas ang eroplano, mas daghang hangin ang modagayday sa pako, busa mas modako ang lift!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They're the very last teeth to grow in, arriving in the late teens or early adulthood
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card only explains the origin of the name 'wisdom teeth' and when they appear. It does not describe how the digestive system (or any listed body system) works, so it provides no direct instructional support for G4-L-1.

copy.en:
Why are they called wisdom teeth?

They're the very last teeth to grow in, arriving in the late teens or early adulthood — an age when a person is supposedly wiser.
copy.tl:
Bakit tinawag na wisdom teeth?

Ito ang pinakahuling ngiping tumutubo, sa panahong binata o dalaga na ang tao — kaya tinawag itong "karunungan" dahil dumarating ito sa mas matalinong edad.
copy.bis:
Nganong gitawag kining wisdom teeth?

Kini ang pinakaulahing ngipon nga moturok, sa panahon nga tin-edyer na o batan-ong hamtong na ang tawo — mao nga gitawag og "kaalam" kay moabot kini sa edad nga mas maalamon na kuno.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wood floats on water because it is lighter than the exact same amount of water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses relative lightness/buoyancy, not the definition of matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. It does not directly support G5-M-1.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wood floats on water because it is lighter than the exact same amount of water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: Floating is a physical property of a solid material, but the competency focuses on properties such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. The card does not directly teach those listed properties.

copy.en: Wood floats on water because it is lighter than the exact same amount of water!
copy.tl: Lumulutang ang kahoy sa tubig dahil mas magaan ito kaysa sa tubig na kasing-laki nito!
copy.bis: Ang kahoy molutaw sa tubig kay mas gaan kini kay sa parehong kadako nga tubig!
